<description>
Kernel logging is inherently global: `KernelLogger` is a process-wide
singleton, so every connection receives every log entry and shares the
minimum level. Multiple `btck_LoggingConnection` handles give the false
impression of independent loggers.

Limit `btck_global_logging_connection_create` to a single connection, so
that the globalness is expressed in that one function and the rest of
the interface can operate on the connection handle.

A single connection also makes it straightforward to invoke the callback
without holding the logger's mutex. Holding it serializes all logging
threads on user code, and deadlocks if anything on the callback's thread
logs, e.g. a garbage collector running finalizers that destroy kernel
objects.

Behaviour changes for consumers:
- `btck_logging_connection_create` is renamed to
  `btck_global_logging_connection_create`, and fails if a connection
  already exists.
- `btck_logging_set_min_level` becomes
  `btck_logging_connection_set_min_level`, and each new connection
  starts at `Info`.
- The "Logger connected." `Debug` entry is removed, since it can no
  longer be delivered.
- The callback can be invoked from multiple threads at the same time,
  so it must be thread-safe. Destroying the connection still waits for
  running invocations to return.
</description>

[2026-10-19] c:6278257737 comment by stickies-v (member):
While working on updating the Python language bindings, I noticed that Python's garbage collection can cause deadlocks even when the logging callback itself wouldn't have caused any deadlocks, because the GC can run finalizers inside the callback, and the (usually `*_destroy`) kernel calls they make log on the same thread. @w0xlt already raised concerns about this too, e.g. [here](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36197#issuecomment-5685155418) and [here](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34374#discussion_r4030551866).

Having a single callback (or one per context, cfr #30342) makes it a lot easier to invoke the callback without holding a lock, so I decided to include that change in this PR too. It comes with the side-effect that log callback invocations are no longer serialized, and callbacks must be thread-safe.

Restructured the commits a bit for reviewability, and also dropped the `MaybeLog` function which didn't really make sense anymore, as `Log` has to be conditional anyway.

I've updated the PR description with the new approach. This PR is now ready for review.
</new_statements>
